F.2.status_claim: implemented and measured locally: content_consumption@1 (KuaiRand random exposure) and the randomised commercial-response models commercial_response@1 (ITT, offline) and ad_exposure_response@1 (E5 redesign: display effect identified with eligibility as the instrument) qualify and beat their baselines on held-out data
F.2.notes: E5 (audit E skeptic S5 REDESIGN): ad_response@2 serves one log-odds shift 1.39 (CI 1.22-1.61) of the displayed individual's own organic visit probability, scaled by attention from a registered attention model per display; incremental visits convert 2.76x (CI 2.03-3.47); no negative effects (none supported by any stratum); transport assumptions documented in RUNTIME.md. ad_response@1 (type table) is superseded and offline only.

F.3.status_claim: implemented; F.3 is no longer slow-only: every qualifying model's held-out test metric is recomputed from the verified datasets through crucible.calibration.runtime (so the runtime is shown to load every kept checkpoint and evaluate held-out rows)
F.3.notes: F.3 recomputes every qualifying model's held-out metric through the runtime, including the E5 model (profile likelihood of the test split through ad_response@2's served predictor). About 20-25 min on one CPU through the slot scheduler.

F.4.status_claim: implemented: every model is compared with simple baselines and, new in this cycle, with the simulator's existing rule-based behaviour on the same held-out rows (E3 reviews for the nine E1/E2 models; rule_comparison in every E4 report)
F.4.notes: Rule-based behaviour scores much worse than the fitted models everywhere it exists (e.g. C2 open rule log loss 0.84 vs 0.44 on KuaiRand random exposure, 0.32 vs 0.15 on MIND; C2 watch rule pinball 0.51 vs 0.13; population rhythm 0.71 vs 0.56 for daily return). The software models have no comparable simulator rule (recorded). Skeptic repair: a comparison counts only when the report agrees with the card (kept candidate, kept and baseline test metrics) and its values are finite; the gate asserts that no kept learned model loses to its baseline (the old test computed but never asserted it).

F.5.notes: NaN or infinite calibration values no longer count as calibration reports (skeptic s2). Equal-width ECE remains the reported measure; at low base rates (MIND 4%) it concentrates rows in one bin (skeptic note) - not changed.

SP-5.5b.status_claim: harness implemented and unit-tested; requirement NOT met: the gate test fails until civ.generate builds and the population records fitted decisions (in_world_validation_reports 0, experiments 0) and until population/models.py stops loading checkpoints directly (out_of_card_scope_uses 1)
SP-5.5b.notes: Model-only driver measured now (KuaiRand 4,026 held-out users, 7 days + 60 beyond): activity TV 0.051 (sessions per active day 0.213: the served C2 constant rate), retention-by-history 0.086, heterogeneity KS 0.051 / sd ratio 0.96, daily-share drift 0.033 and +0.061 over 60 days beyond the data; 1 of 4 within the prespecified tolerances. Honest reading: the fitted return model plus the review-kept constant session rate do not reproduce session heterogeneity and drift upward under their own feedback beyond a week.

limitations: No world consumes any fitted model by default; the population wiring (D-15) is not done. SP-5.0 and SP-5.5b fail (never skip) until it is, and until civ.generate builds again.

The in-world randomised experiments need world mechanisms that do not exist yet: a platform that inserts random items into feeds and labels them, and an ad mechanism that displays campaigns to the population with randomised eligibility. inworld.py analyses their recorded decisions (contract in RUNTIME.md).

ad_response@2: the display shift is that of Criteo's targeted displays on users its bidder reached (exposure 0.1-15% of eligible users, rising with the baseline score); the attention composition, A_ref = 1, frequency saturation and the absence of wear-out/annoyance are assumptions (record advertising.attention_composition); the shift transports across the publisher's sub-sampling only if that sampling depended on the outcome or the arm; the conversion ratio 2.76 reflects retargeting-style high-intent users.

The E5 strata's complier baselines are moment estimates; the joint likelihood recovers a known shift on synthetic trials within 0.2 at the real data's size, but the per-stratum shifts of the low strata are very uncertain (intervals up to 7 log-odds wide).
Model-only validation: 1 of 4 reports within tolerance (sessions per active day, retention by history and drift outside); the fitted return model drifts upward beyond the data's week.
MIND licence acceptance is a user decision (BLOCKERS B-1); news_click@1 and news_click_semantic@1 remain non-commercial research artifacts.
